title: Require memory header, list bad ones
body:
## Goal

Make wrap-up write the memory-file header Claude Code reads (`name`, `description`, `metadata.type`), and make `list-drift.py` list a file whose header is missing or wrong, so no memory file lands headerless again. Owner approved the finding (https://github.com/kalaluthien/mumu-claude-plugin/issues/1148). Prior work: #433 and #446 (wrap-up merge) and #1094 (memory home); none set a header.

- Cause: `homework/skills/wrap-up/SKILL.md` Domain **Memory file** defines the body lines only, and `references/retro.md` step 5 **Add** names only `confirmed` and `last-confirmed`.
- A bad header is: no frontmatter; a `name` that differs from the file name without `.md`; no `description`; a `metadata.type` that is not `user`, `feedback`, `project` or `reference`.
- Scope: the SKILL.md line, the retro.md **Add** line, `scripts/list-drift.py` with a reader in `homework/lib/memory.py`, and a fixture pool in `homework/skills/wrap-up/fixtures/header-pool/`. `MEMORY.md` is not a memory file and stays unchecked.
- Order: #1149 waits on this task.

## Definition of done

1. [check] **Skill names the header**: `grep -c 'metadata.type' homework/skills/wrap-up/SKILL.md` prints `1`; on base `0`.
2. [check] **Add step names the header**: `grep -c 'metadata.type' homework/skills/wrap-up/references/retro.md` prints `1`; on base `0`.
3. [check] **Headerless file listed**: `python3 homework/skills/wrap-up/scripts/list-drift.py /nonexistent homework/skills/wrap-up/fixtures/header-pool 2>&1 | grep -c 'bad header: .*headerless.md'` prints `1`; on base `0`.
4. [check] **Wrong name listed**: `python3 homework/skills/wrap-up/scripts/list-drift.py /nonexistent homework/skills/wrap-up/fixtures/header-pool 2>&1 | grep -c 'bad header: .*wrong-name.md.*name'` prints `1`; on base `0`.
5. [check] **Missing description listed**: `python3 homework/skills/wrap-up/scripts/list-drift.py /nonexistent homework/skills/wrap-up/fixtures/header-pool 2>&1 | grep -c 'bad header: .*no-description.md.*description'` prints `1`; on base `0`.
6. [check] **Bad type listed**: `python3 homework/skills/wrap-up/scripts/list-drift.py /nonexistent homework/skills/wrap-up/fixtures/header-pool 2>&1 | grep -c 'bad header: .*bad-type.md.*metadata.type'` prints `1`; on base `0`.
7. [check] **Only the bad files listed**: `python3 homework/skills/wrap-up/scripts/list-drift.py /nonexistent homework/skills/wrap-up/fixtures/header-pool 2>&1 | grep -c 'bad header'` prints `5`; on base `0`.
8. [check] **Pool holds the files that must pass**: `ls homework/skills/wrap-up/fixtures/header-pool/good.md homework/skills/wrap-up/fixtures/header-pool/blank-line.md homework/skills/wrap-up/fixtures/header-pool/MEMORY.md 2>/dev/null | wc -l` prints `3`; on base `0`.

9. [check] **Index stays headerless**: `test -f homework/skills/wrap-up/fixtures/header-pool/MEMORY.md && grep -c "^---" homework/skills/wrap-up/fixtures/header-pool/MEMORY.md` prints `0`; on base nothing.

10. [check] **Retro runs the check**: `grep -c 'bad header' homework/skills/wrap-up/references/retro.md` prints `1`; on base `0`.
11. [check] **Real memory raises no alarm**: `python3 homework/skills/wrap-up/scripts/list-drift.py ~/.claude ~/.claude/memory ~/.claude/memory/*/ homework/skills/wrap-up/fixtures/header-pool 2>&1 | grep -c 'bad header'` prints `5`; on base `0`.
12. [check] **Type under another key listed**: `python3 homework/skills/wrap-up/scripts/list-drift.py /nonexistent homework/skills/wrap-up/fixtures/header-pool 2>&1 | grep -c 'bad header: .*outside-metadata.md.*metadata.type'` prints `1`; on base `0`.

title: Guard git landing, place worktrees
body:
## Goal

Stop a git landing from reporting success while the base checkout stays behind, and put a worker's worktree beside the others, from the outside projects' requests in https://github.com/kalaluthien/mumu-claude-plugin/issues/1133 (`landing-bare-report.md`: two landings moved `main` while the files stayed old for two hours; `repeated-mistakes.md` section 2: 3 sessions made the worktree under a plugin subfolder).

- **Bare flag**: `landing_git.merge()` refuses, changing nothing, when `core.bare` is true on a repository whose common folder is a `.git`, since no worktree then shows as holding the base, and the error says `git config core.bare false`. A truly bare repository still lands by `update-ref`. Their `git init` cause is theirs to fix.
- **Worktree place**: a new `teamwork/skills/kick-off/scripts/add-worktree.py <name> <base> [<branch>]` runs `git worktree add` at the main checkout's `.claude/worktrees/<name>` from any folder, and prints the path; both landing adapters' `branch` rows name it.
- **Not here**: the reflog message of the `update-ref` path; `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` (section 3).
- Files: `teamwork/lib/landing_git.py`, `teamwork/skills/kick-off/fixtures/replay-landing-scenario.py`, new `add-worktree.py`, `references/adapters/landing-git.md`, `landing-github.md`.



## Definition of done

1. [check] **a bare flag refuses the merge**: `python3 teamwork/skills/kick-off/fixtures/replay-landing-scenario.py 2>&1 | grep -c '^ok refuse-bare-checkout$'` prints `1`, a merge with `core.bare` true exiting 1, naming `core.bare`, and leaving the base and the change as they were; on base `0`.
2. [check] **the worktree lands at the main checkout**: `S=$PWD/teamwork/skills/kick-off/scripts; d=$(mktemp -d) && git -C $d init -q -b main && git -C $d commit -q --allow-empty -m i && mkdir $d/sub && (cd $d/sub && python3 $S/add-worktree.py probe-worker main >/dev/null 2>&1); test -d $d/.claude/worktrees/probe-worker && ! test -e $d/sub/.claude && echo root || echo misplaced` prints `root`; on base `misplaced`.
3. [check] **a branch name is kept**: `S=$PWD/teamwork/skills/kick-off/scripts; d=$(mktemp -d) && git -C $d init -q -b main && git -C $d commit -q --allow-empty -m i && (cd $d && python3 $S/add-worktree.py probe-worker main feature/probe-worker >/dev/null 2>&1); git -C $d branch --list feature/probe-worker | grep -c feature/probe-worker` prints `1`; on base `0`.
4. [check] **both adapters name the script**: `cat teamwork/skills/kick-off/references/adapters/landing-git.md teamwork/skills/kick-off/references/adapters/landing-github.md | grep -c 'add-worktree.py'` prints `2`; on base `0`.
5. [check] **no replay step fails and the bare clone is left alone**: `python3 teamwork/skills/kick-off/fixtures/replay-landing-scenario.py 2>&1 | grep -c '^ok '` prints `11`, every step ok including `bare-repository`, a truly bare clone not flagged by the guard; on base `9`.

title: Remove manager self-exit protocol
body:
## Goal

Remove the manager's self-exit protocol from the teamwork plugin, so a manager ends only when the owner tells it to end itself or ends it by hand (https://github.com/kalaluthien/mumu-claude-plugin/issues/1137).

- After this work the owner decides when a manager ends, and no heartbeat line or peer proposal ends one.
- What it does: deletes the heartbeat `exit` line and the code that feeds it, deletes manager.md step 5's exit proposal and `OK` answer, drops manager.md step 5's `compact` rule kept for an objection, drops `team_names.workers`, whose only caller was the exit block, drops the herdr `close` row's trace of a self-ended session, and says in manager.md that a manager closes itself only on the owner's word.
- Undoes #469, #477 / PR #478, #606, #1002; read: each landed to end an idle manager by agreement and keep one live, which the owner now rejects.
- Keeps: the other heartbeat lines (`idle`, `route`, `feed`), the `close` of an idle worker, Succession, and the sentinel's `Manager ends` rule, since a manager still ends by the owner's word.
- Scope: `teamwork/` only; no new mechanism.

## Definition of done

1. [check] **No exit protocol left**: `grep -rnE "exit_action|had_worker|propose your exit|OK to |exit once" teamwork --include=*.py --include=*.md --include=*.json | wc -l | tr -d ' '` prints 0; on base 15.
2. [check] **Monitor read keeps only me and since**: `python3 -c "import inspect,sys; sys.path.insert(0,'teamwork/lib'); import team_gaps; print(sorted(inspect.signature(team_gaps.manager_read).parameters)==['me', 'since'])"` prints True; on base False.
3. [check] **Owner's word ends the manager**: `grep -c "close yourself only when the owner" teamwork/skills/kick-off/references/manager.md` prints 1; on base 0.
4. [check] **Exit-only helper gone**: `grep -c "def workers" teamwork/lib/team_names.py` prints 0; on base 1.
5. [check] **Objection rule gone**: `grep -c "Kept alive" teamwork/skills/kick-off/references/manager.md` prints 0; on base 1.
6. [check] **Monitor still loads and reads**: `python3 -c "import runpy; print(runpy.run_path('teamwork/monitors/print-team-gaps.py')['read'].__code__.co_argcount==3)"` prints True; on base False.

checks.command: grep -rnE "exit_action|had_worker|propose your exit|OK to |exit once" teamwork --include=*.py --include=*.md --include=*.json | wc -l | tr -d ' '

title: Nest tasks under the nearest backlog
body:
## Goal

Make `nest` put a task under the nearest backlog at or above the issue named, and refuse when none is above it, so a task can no longer hide under another task, with no extra step for the reader, as the owner asked in https://github.com/kalaluthien/mumu-claude-plugin/issues/1037 (structural, not a patch; fewer moving parts and tokens).

- **Cause**: `worker.md:12` says nest "under the backlog", but a worker started with a task url nests under that task; nothing reads the target's labels (`teamwork/skills/kick-off/scripts/use-board.py:52-53`, `teamwork/lib/board_files.py:138-142`, `teamwork/lib/board_github.py:306-307`), and the backlog pane shows direct children only, so infra-landscape tasks #58 and #59 under task #57 were hidden.
- **Choice removed**: the board port's `nest` walks the parent chain from the issue named to the first one labelled `backlog` and nests there, in one place for every board adapter (`teamwork/lib/board.py`); with none, it raises and writes nothing. Fix A of the backlog: the worker's url stays valid, and no start-time or label check is added.
- **One command on both boards**: `board-github.md`'s `nest` row becomes `use-board.py nest <issue> <task>`, as the files board already does, dropping its two-call id lookup.
- `protocol.md`'s `nest` row and `worker.md:12` say it in the same words, `nearest backlog at or above`.



## Definition of done

1. [check] **task under a task lands on the backlog**: `python3 teamwork/skills/kick-off/fixtures/replay-nest-target.py 2>/dev/null | grep -c '^under-task pass$'` prints `1`; on base `0`, since the script is new. On a temporary files board it files a backlog, a task nested under it, and a second task nested under the first task; the second's parent, read back by `use-board.py read`, must be the backlog for the line to say `pass`.
2. [check] **no backlog above refused**: `python3 teamwork/skills/kick-off/fixtures/replay-nest-target.py 2>/dev/null | grep -c '^no-backlog pass$'` prints `1`; on base `0`. Nesting under an issue with no backlog at or above it must exit 1, and `use-board.py read` must show the task with no parent.
3. [check] **GitHub nest by the port**: `grep -c 'use-board.py nest' teamwork/skills/kick-off/references/adapters/board-github.md` prints `1`; on base `0`.
4. [check] **id lookup dropped**: `grep -c 'sub_issues' teamwork/skills/kick-off/references/adapters/board-github.md` prints `0`; on base `1`.
5. [check] **walk in the port**: `grep -c '^def nest' teamwork/lib/board.py` prints `1`; on base `0`. Both adapters keep their own `nest`, reached only through it; a live run on kalaluthien/teamwork-board-sandbox, posted as a `REPORTED:`, shows the GitHub board follows the walk.
6. [check] **same words**: `grep -l 'nearest backlog at or above' teamwork/skills/kick-off/references/protocol.md teamwork/skills/kick-off/references/worker.md | wc -l | tr -d ' '` prints `2`; on base `0`.

checks.command: grep -l 'nearest backlog at or above' teamwork/skills/kick-off/references/protocol.md teamwork/skills/kick-off/references/worker.md | wc -l | tr -d ' '

title: Reopen and retitle on the files board
body:
## Goal

Make the files board (`TEAMWORK_BOARD=files`) follow the GitHub board's usage pattern, reopening a closed backlog or task first, as the owner asked in https://github.com/kalaluthien/mumu-claude-plugin/issues/1022.

- **Reopen**: a `reopen` board operation in `protocol.md`'s table, a row in both board adapters, `board_files.reopen` and `board_github.reopen`, and `use-board.py reopen <issue>`; on both boards a reopened issue reads `state: OPEN`, `stateReason: REOPENED`, `closedAt: None`, as GitHub answers (sandbox probe on `kalaluthien/teamwork-board-sandbox#42`: `["open","reopened",null]`). `manager.md`'s closed-backlog row names `reopen`, since it says "reopen that backlog" with no operation behind it today.
- **Retitle**: `manager.md` rewrites a backlog's title at each material scope change; `board-github.md` does it by `gh issue edit --title`, the files board has no way. Add `use-board.py title <issue> <title>` on both boards, named in both adapters' `edit` rows, its title length read by `board_files.command`, so the title hook guards it as it guards `gh issue edit --title`.
- **Refusals as GitHub refuses**: sandbox probes (`kalaluthien/teamwork-board-sandbox#42`-`#48`) showed GitHub refuse, each 422 unless named: a second parent (`Sub issue may only have one parent`, the same parent again included), an issue nested under itself (`Sub issue cannot be the same as the parent issue`), an issue blocked by itself (`Target issue cannot be the same as the source issue`), the same blocker twice (`Target issue has already been taken`), and removing a label the issue lacks (`Label does not exist`, 404); it accepts adding a label twice (kept once) and reopening an open issue (`already open`, exit 0, `state_reason` unchanged). The files board accepts each refused case silently today (`teamwork/lib/board_files.py:123-133`). Each refuses on the files board, writing nothing; a missing issue stays refused, as today.
- **Scenario**: `fixtures/replay-board-scenario.py` gains the steps `retitle`, `reopen` (the resolved backlog), `nest-again` (a new task under it) and `resolve-again`, so the same-result diff covers the new scenario on both boards.
- **Hook sees the new writes**: `board_files.command` matches `use-board.py reopen` and `use-board.py title`, as `board_github.command` matches any `gh issue` write, so the hook's title guard and reminders reach them.
- Builds on #865 (files board, scenario) and #1019/#1020 (board setting read).



## Definition of done

1. 2. [check] **files board reopens**: `d=$(mktemp -d); echo b > $d/b; echo 'REPORTED: done' > $d/r; export TEAMWORK_BOARD=files TEAMWORK_BOARD_DIR=$d/board HOME=$d; U=teamwork/skills/kick-off/scripts/use-board.py; python3 $U file T $d/b >/dev/null; python3 $U resolve 1 $d/r; python3 $U reopen 1 2>/dev/null; python3 -c 'import sys; sys.path[:0] = ["teamwork/lib"]; import board; i = board.fresh(1); print(i["state"], i["stateReason"], i["closedAt"] is None)'` prints `OPEN REOPENED True`; on base `CLOSED COMPLETED False`.
3. [check] **files board retitles**: `d=$(mktemp -d); echo b > $d/b; export TEAMWORK_BOARD=files TEAMWORK_BOARD_DIR=$d/board HOME=$d; U=teamwork/skills/kick-off/scripts/use-board.py; python3 $U file Old $d/b >/dev/null; python3 $U title 1 New 2>/dev/null; python3 $U read 1 | head -1 | cut -d' ' -f2` prints `New`; on base `Old`.
4. [check] **refused as GitHub refuses**: `d=$(mktemp -d); echo b > $d/b; export TEAMWORK_BOARD=files TEAMWORK_BOARD_DIR=$d/board HOME=$d; U=teamwork/skills/kick-off/scripts/use-board.py; for t in A B C D; do python3 $U file $t $d/b >/dev/null; done; python3 $U nest 1 3; python3 $U order 1 2; { for c in 'nest 2 3' 'nest 1 3' 'nest 4 4' 'order 1 1' 'order 1 2' 'order 1 9' 'label 1 nolabel --remove'; do python3 $U $c; echo $?; done; python3 -c 'import sys, json; m = lambda n: json.load(open(f"{sys.argv[1]}/{n}/issue.json")); print(m(3)["parent"], m(4)["parent"], m(1)["blockers"])' $d/board; } 2>/dev/null | paste -sd' ' -` prints `1 1 1 1 1 1 1 1 None [2]`; on base `0 0 0 0 0 1 0 1 4 [1, 2]`.
5. [check] **title hook reads use-board**: `python3 -c 'import sys; sys.path[:0] = ["teamwork/lib"]; import board_files; c = board_files.command("use-board.py title 3 \"" + "x" * 41 + "\""); print(c and c["title"])'` prints `41`; on base `None`.
6. [check] **reopen and title documented**: `` R=teamwork/skills/kick-off/references; { for f in protocol.md adapters/board-github.md adapters/board-files.md; do grep -q '^| .*`reopen`' $R/$f || echo "no reopen $f"; done; grep '^| `edit`' $R/adapters/board-files.md | grep -q 'use-board.py title' || echo 'no title'; grep 'closed backlog' $R/manager.md | grep -q '`reopen`' || echo 'no manager'; } | wc -l | tr -d ' ' `` prints `0`; on base `5`.

title: Run criteria on a pass sample
body:
Make `run-criteria.py` able to run each `[check]` on a sample of its expected pass, so a check that can never pass is caught before the task is filed.

- Lesson (memory `pitfall-unrun-criterion-command`, confirmed 6 times): run every `[check]` command on its pass path before filing, not only on the base.
- Repeat 2026-10-24, #840: criterion 1 passed `run-criteria.py --base`, then failed at the head with a traceback, since `check-schema.py check /dev/stdin` reads a valid document twice: https://github.com/kalaluthien/mumu-claude-plugin/issues/840#issuecomment-6379112301.
- Proposal: a check step, not a written rule, such as a `--pass <sample-file>` mode that substitutes a sample for the command's input, or a lint warning on `/dev/stdin` in a command.


## Goal

Make `run-criteria.py` run a `[check]` on a sample of its pass (owner's words above), and say `unclear` when it cannot split the command surely.

## Definition of done

2. title: Keep concurrent files-board writes
body:
## Goal

Stop the files board (`TEAMWORK_BOARD=files`, `teamwork/lib/board_files.py`) from losing or breaking records when sessions write at once. The owner chose this on 2026-11-04 (https://github.com/kalaluthien/mumu-claude-plugin/issues/1161, newest `DECIDED:`: "fix the files board's lost concurrent writes now").

- **Found by**: the research on #1161 (https://github.com/kalaluthien/mumu-claude-plugin/issues/1161#issuecomment-6607688424, finding 2). Re-measured on base `ff2d643`, each round 40 processes at once:
  - comments: 38–39 of 40 kept, while their writers exit 0;
  - new issues: 35–40 of 40 filed;
  - labels on one issue: 17–29 of 40 kept;
  - in 2 of 9 rounds, `1/issue.json` was left unparseable (`JSONDecodeError: Extra data`), which blinds every read of the board.
- **Causes**:
  - `comment()` numbers by `len(glob) + 1`, and `write_text` overwrites a file another writer just made.
  - `file()` numbers by `max + 1`.
  - `save()` reads `issue.json`, changes it and writes it back with no lock, so concurrent writers lose each other's fields; `write_text` truncates in place, so two writers interleave bytes.
- **Scope**: every write of `board_files.py` (`comment`, `file`, `edit`, `resolve`, `reopen`, `retitle`, `order`, `nest`, `label`) runs as one locked step, and every file it writes appears whole to a reader. Records, paths, urls, the GitHub board and the board port keep their shape. Readers take no lock.
- **Shape kept**: the files-board replays (`replay-board-scenario.py --board files`, `replay-nest-target.py`, `replay-files-pane.py`, `replay-data-folder.py`, `replay-board-setting.py` in `teamwork/skills/kick-off/fixtures/`) print the same at the head as on the base, run before each judge; no `[check]` states it, since a check that nothing changed passes on the base.
- **Not in scope**: the store choice and the remote push, both still open on #1161; the git hook, which the owner declined; a reader that skips a hand-broken file.



## Definition of done

1. [check] **no concurrent write lost**: `F=$(mktemp -d); U=teamwork/skills/kick-off/scripts/use-board.py; echo b > $F/b; lost=0; for r in 1 2 3; do export TEAMWORK_BOARD=files TEAMWORK_BOARD_DIR=$F/$r HOME=$F CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR=$F; python3 $U file T $F/b >/dev/null; seq 40 | xargs -P 40 -I{} python3 $U comment 1 $F/b >/dev/null 2>&1; seq 40 | xargs -P 40 -I{} python3 $U file T{} $F/b >/dev/null 2>&1; seq 40 | xargs -P 40 -I{} python3 $U label 1 L{} >/dev/null 2>&1; n=$(python3 -c 'import json, pathlib, sys; b = pathlib.Path(sys.argv[1]); print(len(list((b / "1/comments").glob("*.md"))), len(list(b.glob("[0-9]*"))) - 1, len(json.loads((b / "1/issue.json").read_text())["labels"]))' $F/$r 2>/dev/null); [ "$n" = "40 40 40" ] || lost=$((lost+1)); done; echo $lost` prints `0`; on base `3`.
2. [check] **other writes keep their effect under concurrency**: `F=$(mktemp -d); U=teamwork/skills/kick-off/scripts/use-board.py; echo b > $F/b; echo 'REPORTED: done' > $F/r; printf -- '--- body\n+++ body\n@@ -1 +1 @@\n-b\n+c\n' > $F/d; { for k in $(seq 4 22); do echo "order 2 $k"; echo "label 2 L$k"; echo "label 3 L$k"; done; echo 'title 2 New'; echo "resolve 2 $F/r"; echo 'nest 1 2'; echo "edit 2 $F/d DECIDED:e"; echo 'reopen 3'; } > $F/ops; lost=0; for r in 1 2 3; do export TEAMWORK_BOARD=files TEAMWORK_BOARD_DIR=$F/$r HOME=$F CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR=$F; for i in $(seq 22); do python3 $U file T $F/b >/dev/null; done; python3 $U label 1 backlog; python3 $U resolve 3 $F/r >/dev/null; xargs -P 62 -L1 python3 $U < $F/ops >/dev/null 2>&1; n=$(python3 -c 'import json, pathlib, sys; b = pathlib.Path(sys.argv[1]); two, three = (json.loads((b / f"{n}/issue.json").read_text()) for n in (2, 3)); print(len(two["blockers"]), len(two["labels"]), two["title"], two["state"], two["parent"], (b / "2/body.md").read_text().strip(), three["state"], len(three["labels"]))' $F/$r 2>/dev/null); [ "$n" = "19 19 New CLOSED 1 c OPEN 19" ] || lost=$((lost+1)); done; echo $lost` prints `0`; on base `3`.
3. [check] **readers never see a half-written file**: `F=$(mktemp -d); U=teamwork/skills/kick-off/scripts/use-board.py; echo b > $F/b; torn=0; for r in 1 2 3; do export TEAMWORK_BOARD=files TEAMWORK_BOARD_DIR=$F/$r HOME=$F CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR=$F; python3 $U file T $F/b >/dev/null; { seq 40 | sed 's/^/label 1 L/'; seq 40 | sed "s|.*|comment 1 $F/b|"; } > $F/ops; { xargs -P 80 -L1 python3 $U < $F/ops; touch $F/done$r; } >/dev/null 2>&1 & n=$(python3 -c "$(printf 'import json, pathlib, sys\nb, done, bad = pathlib.Path(sys.argv[1]), pathlib.Path(sys.argv[2]), 0\nwhile not done.exists():\n    try:\n        json.loads((b / "1/issue.json").read_text()); bad += not all(path.read_text() for path in [b / "1/body.md", *(b / "1/comments").glob("*.md")])\n    except (ValueError, OSError):\n        bad += 1\nprint(bad)')" $F/$r $F/done$r); wait; [ "$n" = 0 ] || torn=$((torn+1)); done; echo $torn` prints `0`; on base `3`.

title: Teach homework the memory home
body:
## Goal

Teach homework the memory home the owner approved in option 5 (https://github.com/kalaluthien/mumu-claude-plugin/issues/1091#issuecomment-6472364490), step 2 of its build order (#issuecomment-6472475621): one root `autoMemoryDirectory` names, whose `MEMORY.md` every session loads, and a folder per repository under it, `<home>/<repo>/`.

- **SessionStart hook**: prints the repository's folder, its index, and one sentence on where a lesson goes; `<repo>` is the origin's name, else the main checkout's folder name, so worktrees and clones share one folder; the home is read from the main checkout's `.claude/settings.local.json`, which Claude Code 2.1.312 reads in each worktree too (probe: https://github.com/kalaluthien/mumu-claude-plugin/issues/1094#issuecomment-6473253475), then `<config>/settings.json`, a `~/` expanded; prints nothing when no `autoMemoryDirectory` is set, and never stops a session.
- **`move-memory.py`**: moves a memory file and its index line between folders, refusing to overwrite.
- **Globs**: `list-drift.py` and `list-repeats.py` read the home and its folders, the home found as the hook finds it from the folder they run in, then `<config>/projects/*/memory/`.
- **retro**: a lesson for every project goes to the home directly, a `CLAUDE.md` patch only with no home; a repository lesson moves to the home once another repository holds it; another repository's folder is still written by patch (#890); a skill lesson stays in memory, marked `skill: <plugin>:<skill>` or `skill: new <name>`.
- **dream**: moves a lesson in the home true for one repository down to its folder, and the reverse; asks the owner per marked lesson, write it, keep it or drop it; a skill of another repository's plugin goes as a `backlog` issue there.
- **README and SKILL.md** name the home, the setting and the flow.
- **Unchanged**: a user with no `autoMemoryDirectory` keeps today's pools.

## Definition of done

title: Rename teamwork code to whole words
body:
## Goal

Make every name in teamwork's code the whole word it stands for, take the cross-plugin names, and drop the one stale fixture, with behaviour kept (owner's words on #1062: "쓰지 않는 playbook이나 관련 스크립트 같은 거 낡은거 전부", https://github.com/kalaluthien/mumu-claude-plugin/issues/1062, and "파일 이름 함수 이름 헤더 이름 개념 이름 일관성이나 규칙 안맞는것도 전수 조사해서 일치시켜. 세 플러그인 각각 + 플러그인 간에 전부", https://github.com/kalaluthien/mumu-claude-plugin/issues/1062#issuecomment-6459763030).

- **Word names**: every Python and TypeScript name under `teamwork/` (variables, parameters, lambdas, functions, attributes, import aliases, TypeScript bindings and `catch` names) is a whole word, as `AGENTS.md` **Word names** says: each `_` or camelCase part is an English word or a standard term of the field (`args`, `stdout`, `worktree`). A lone `n`, `k`, `e` or `i` stays only for a count, key, error or index, so an `i`, `n`, `k` or `e` that holds anything else (an issue, an issue number, a session name, a node, an event), as a parameter, a loop target or an assignment, takes the whole word; the plugin API's `$` stays. About 344 names and 91 letters, listed by the first two criteria's commands.
- **Cross-plugin names**: teamwork's rows of the names list (https://github.com/kalaluthien/mumu-claude-plugin/issues/1062#issuecomment-6459949094): `INSTALL`, `missing` and `need` move from `lib/json_command.py` to `lib/install_line.py`; `lint-criteria.py` becomes `check-criteria.py`; each self-check (the six `replay-*.py` beside `probe-tell-session.py`, not `replay-board-scenario.py`, which prints a board dump) prints `ok <name>` or `fail <name>: <detail>` through a `step` helper.
- **One word, one meaning**: `session_gaps.stamp(text)`, which parses a time, takes a name saying so, since `stamp` elsewhere makes an ISO time (`board_files.py:25`, `landing_git.py:24`) or reads a signal file (`team_signal.py:7`).
- **Script form**: each script, and each Python fixture (`probe-tell-session.py`, `replay-data-folder.py` and `replay-files-pane.py` run on with `--x` today), answers an unknown option, and a call with no argument when each of its `usage:` lines needs one, with its docstring on stderr and exit 2 (`AGENTS.md` **Script form**), and so do the scripts the issue pane and Claude Code's monitor run (`hooks/list-issue-board.py`, `hooks/wait-team-change.py`, `monitors/print-team-gaps.py`), while `hooks/route-event.py`, a hook, keeps its exit codes; option-parsing scripts go through one parser in a new `lib/usage_parser.py` rather than a copy per script, and each flag a script's `usage:` line names is lowercase whole words (`list-session-gaps.py --from-dir` becomes `--from-folder`); `rename-session.py` today renames the session to any argument, `--x` included. Each script, hook, monitor and fixture docstring opens with a verb in the imperative, as most do (`list-sessions.py` and `print-scope-label.py` open with "Prints", `route-event.py` with "Timing-bound steps live", `fake-herdr/herdr` with "A stand-in"). Each script and fixture reaches a path beside it through `HERE` or `ROOT` (`replay-nest-target.py` builds `parents[1] / "scripts"` inline).
- **File names**: each script's name opens with a verb (`AGENTS.md` **Names**, "a hook's included"): `hooks/issue-pane.tsx`, the module `hooks.json` loads, becomes `hooks/draw-issue-pane.tsx`, with its four references; `fake-herdr/herdr` and `recorded-gh/gh` keep the name of the tool they stand in for, a name the tool fixes.
- **Stale file**: `fixtures/fake-gh/gh` goes: no script or document names it or its `FAKE_GH_LOG` (`git grep -n "fake-gh\|FAKE_GH_LOG"` finds only the file itself). The `.md` fixtures stay: they are the documents `lint-criteria.py` and `run-criteria.py` must accept or reject, which **No tests or evals** allows, and each still gives its verdict at 5abee22. `fixtures/pass-sample-input.txt` stays, though no file names it: it is the sample `run-criteria.py --pass <n>=fixtures/pass-sample-input.txt fixtures/pass-sample.md` feeds each pipe split, the `--pass` probe #857 kept, run by hand. Every other teamwork file is named by another file, a loader, or is such a fixture.
- **Behaviour kept**: no output of any hook, monitor or script changes but the usage text; the fixtures replay as on the base. `compare-team-output.py` covers the hooks, the board, the heartbeat and the scripts its jobs name; a second guard runs the rest (the criteria checker on each `.md` fixture, `list-session-gaps.py`, `backtest-estimate.py` on a saved history, `run-on-refs.py`, `wait-team-change.py`) at the head and on the base.
- **Not here**: Markdown headers and words, which #1077 changes after this task lands; here Markdown changes only where it names a renamed file (`worker.md:14`); `gaps` stays in both `team_gaps` (missing work) and `session_gaps` (idle time), as plain English for both.

## Goal

Make every session script find a session through herdr on each call, so a pane herdr moves (such as `w9:p1` to `w4:pF`) keeps rename, tell, close, answer and start working, as the owner asked in https://github.com/kalaluthien/mumu-claude-plugin/issues/1034.

- **Stale value**: a shell's `HERDR_PANE_ID` keeps the pane it started in. `session_herdr.sessions` found "this session" by it (`teamwork/lib/session_herdr.py:18`), so after a move the heartbeat, `rename-session.py`, `close-session.py`'s own check and `print-scope-label.py --me` read another session, or none. A live read on 2026-10-26 with `HERDR_PANE_ID` set to the manager's pane: origin/main took this worker for `teamwork-manager`.
- **Own session by id**: herdr lists each Claude session's id as `agent_session.value`, and it equals the session's `CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID`, the monitor's too (read by `ps eww` on the live heartbeat). Find this session by that id first, and use the pane only when herdr lists no id.
- **Name as target**: `herdr agent prompt|read|send-keys|wait` take the agent's name and resolve it on each call, as `session-herdr.md`'s `LOOK` already uses. Every agent call after a start targets the name, never a pane id kept from an earlier read: `start-session.py`, `close-session.py`, `rename-session.py`, `answer-prompt.py`'s read and `message_herdr`.
- **Pane-only commands**: `pane send-text`, `tab rename` and `pane rename` take only an id, so each reads it from herdr right before the call.
- `open_tab` drops its fallback to the caller's `HERDR_PANE_ID`, which no script uses since #1032.
- Builds on #1032 (https://github.com/kalaluthien/mumu-claude-plugin/pull/1033).



## Definition of done

1. [check] **own session after a move**: `python3 teamwork/skills/kick-off/fixtures/replay-team-scenarios.py --only moved-me | grep -c '^moved-me pass$'` prints `1`; on base `0`. The scenario's `HERDR_PANE_ID` names another manager's pane, and `print-scope-label.py --me` must still print this session's label. With no session id listed, the pane it started in must still find it. It stands for every caller of `session.sessions()`, the heartbeat's included (`teamwork/monitors/print-team-gaps.py:43`), since each reads "this session" only there.
2. [check] **each script after a move**: `python3 teamwork/skills/kick-off/fixtures/replay-team-scenarios.py --only moved-close,moved-tell,moved-answer,moved-rename,moved-start | grep -cE '^moved-(close|tell|answer|rename|start) pass$'` prints `5`; on base `0`. In each scenario the target's pane moves after the read that found it. Then `close-session.py` must answer its dialog and close it, `tell-session.py` must deliver, `answer-prompt.py` must answer at the new pane, `rename-session.py` must rename it in herdr and in its transcript, and `start-session.py` must get its kick-off taken. With origin/main's scripts and these fixtures, all five fail.
3. [check] **no caller-pane fallback**: `grep -c 'pane", "get"' teamwork/lib/session_herdr.py` prints `0`; on base `1`.

title: Follow a board setting written late
body:
## Goal

Make the issue pane and the heartbeat read the board the project's settings name, even when a process started before the setting was written, as the owner asked: "Fix the ordering bug in which the Mod and heartbeat read GitHub issues or local files" (https://github.com/kalaluthien/mumu-claude-plugin/issues/1019).

- **Settings read at each call**: `teamwork/lib/board.py` and `landing.py` pick their adapter at each use, from `TEAMWORK_BOARD` / `TEAMWORK_LANDING` in the environment, else from the `env` of the project's `.claude/settings.local.json`, then `settings.json`, in the current git root, then the main checkout (a worktree has no local settings). This is fix option (b) of #1019; option (a), a manager restart by Succession, is set aside, since it fixes only the manager's processes and only when the manager remembers it.
- **Heartbeat follows a change**: `teamwork/monitors/print-team-gaps.py`, seeing the board or landing change, drops its last read and touches the signal file, so the issue pane reads the board again too.
- **Plain output**: the board read failure names the board kind (`list-issue-board.py`); the pane says "No board read yet." before a read worked and "The board has no open issues." after; `monitors.json` no longer calls the heartbeat GitHub-only.
- **Manager step**: `kick-off/references/manager.md` step 1 no longer asks to export the pick in the shell, since every script reads the settings file.
- **Kept**: the team and landing scenarios still pass, and the pane still builds; the change's judge runs them, since they pass on base too.
- **Not here**: a setting changed while the environment variable is set (the environment wins, as in Claude Code); the session, agent ports.
- Builds on #984 (board choice at manager start, https://github.com/kalaluthien/mumu-claude-plugin/pull/985), #933 (git landing) and #862 (ports).
- Files: new `teamwork/lib/port_setting.py`, `teamwork/lib/board.py`, `teamwork/lib/landing.py`, `teamwork/monitors/print-team-gaps.py`, `teamwork/monitors/monitors.json`, `teamwork/hooks/list-issue-board.py`, `teamwork/hooks/issue-pane.tsx`, `teamwork/types/index.d.ts`, `teamwork/skills/kick-off/references/manager.md`, new `teamwork/skills/kick-off/fixtures/replay-board-setting.py`, new `teamwork/hooks/fixtures/render-empty-pane.ts`.



## Definition of done

1. [check] **pane woken**: `python3 teamwork/skills/kick-off/fixtures/replay-board-setting.py 2>&1 | grep -c '^ok signal$'` prints `1`, a manager heartbeat started with no setting touching the signal file the pane waits on once `settings.local.json` names the files board; on base `0`.
2. [check] **heartbeat follows a late landing**: `python3 teamwork/skills/kick-off/fixtures/replay-board-setting.py 2>&1 | grep -c '^ok late-landing$'` prints `1`, the heartbeat routing nothing while its landing reads a failing GitHub, and `TEAMWORK_LANDING=git` written later alone touching the signal file again; on base `0`.
3. [check] **heartbeat follows a late setting**: `python3 teamwork/skills/kick-off/fixtures/replay-board-setting.py 2>&1 | grep -c '^ok late-setting$'` prints `1`, the heartbeat then routing the files board's backlog, never routed before; on base `0`.
4. [check] **worktree reads main settings**: `python3 teamwork/skills/kick-off/fixtures/replay-board-setting.py 2>&1 | grep -c '^ok worktree$'` prints `1`; on base `0`.
5. [check] **environment wins**: `python3 teamwork/skills/kick-off/fixtures/replay-board-setting.py 2>&1 | grep -c '^ok environment-wins$'` prints `1`; on base `0`.
6. [check] **failure names the board**: `python3 teamwork/skills/kick-off/fixtures/replay-board-setting.py 2>&1 | grep -c '^ok failure-names-board$'` prints `1`; on base `0`.
7. [check] **empty told from not read**: `bun teamwork/hooks/fixtures/render-empty-pane.ts 2>&1 | grep -cxE 'unread: No board read yet\.|empty: The board has no open issues\.'` prints `2`, the pane rendered before any read and after a good read of no issues; on base `0`.
8. [check] **heartbeat not GitHub-only**: `grep -c GitHub teamwork/monitors/monitors.json` prints `0`; on base `1`.
9. [check] **no shell export step**: `grep -c 'export it in your shell' teamwork/skills/kick-off/references/manager.md` prints `0`; on base `1`.
